production_notes: [REGION] [VERIFY] Rules requiring customers to be told they are talking to AI (for example the EU AI Act transparency obligations) and local data protection laws such as the GDPR. The voiceover keeps AI disclosure and data protection as principles only and names no law; if a reviewer confirms the wording, the law names may appear on the lesson page, not in the video.
Judgement call carried from curriculum: no industry benchmark figures or target numbers for support metrics. Slides must show no percentages or targets; any benchmark added later needs [VERIFY].

Sofie and the Ghent bicycle rental company are fictional; the 'twenty random conversations each week' and 'two-month pilot' are her own plan, not benchmarks. Stock footage must show no real rental brand names or logos.

Hook.voiceover: Imagine your new assistant handles almost every conversation without a person. It looks like a great result. But what if many of those customers simply gave up and closed the chat? The numbers you choose decide what you see.

Explain.voiceover: In the last lesson, you tested your assistant before launch. In this final lesson, we look at how to measure it after launch, and how to keep the human touch. Four measures are useful for most support assistants.

slide.title: Measuring Success and Keeping the Human Touch
slide.body: AI for Customer Experience and Support · Lesson 12 of 12 · Capstone step 4

Explain.voiceover: First response time is how long a customer waits for the first useful reply. But a fast wrong answer is not a success. Resolution rate is the share of conversations where the problem was actually solved. You can ask, did this answer your question, or check if the customer contacted you again soon.

slide.title: Measures 1 and 2
slide.body: 1. First response time: wait for the first useful reply. 2. Resolution rate: problem actually solved ('Did this answer your question?' · no repeat contact soon after).

Explain.voiceover: Hand-off rate is the share of conversations passed to a person. A hand-off is not a failure. The question is whether the right conversations are handed off. And customer satisfaction is a short rating at the end, for both AI-only and handed-off conversations.

slide.title: Measures 3 and 4
slide.body: 3. Hand-off rate: are the right conversations handed off? 4. Customer satisfaction: short rating for AI-only and handed-off conversations.

Explain.voiceover: This course gives no target numbers. Good values depend on your industry, customers and channels. Compare with your own team's results before launch, and follow the trend. And keep checking the points from lesson eleven: accuracy, tone, fairness across languages, and privacy.
Explain.on_screen_text: Compare with yourself, not a benchmark

Explain.voiceover: Always read the measures together. The rate of conversations that never reach a person is sometimes called containment. If customers leave without an answer, containment goes up, while satisfaction and resolution go down. Watch for warning signs: chats that end suddenly, repeat contacts by email or phone, and low ratings after AI-only chats.

slide.title: Containment can mislead
slide.body: Arrow up: Containment. Arrows down: Satisfaction, Resolution. Warning signs: chats that end suddenly · repeat contacts by email or phone · low ratings after AI-only chats.

Explain.voiceover: Privacy and transparency are principles, not extras. Tell customers they are talking to AI, and how to reach a person. Collect only the data you need, follow the data protection rules where your customers live, and ask your legal team before any real launch. And keep real customer data out of free test tools.

slide.title: Principles, not extras
slide.body: Tell customers it's AI + how to reach a person · collect only the data you need · follow local data protection rules; ask your legal team · no real customer data in free test tools

Explain.voiceover: Think of a doctor checking a patient. A normal temperature with a very high heart rate still means something is wrong. In the same way, high containment with low satisfaction means customers are not being helped.
Explain.stock_query: doctor checking patient heart rate monitor
Explain.on_screen_text: Look at all the signs together

Demonstrate.voiceover: Let's see a launch note. Sofie runs support for a hypothetical bicycle rental company in Ghent, Belgium. Customers write in Dutch, French and English. She prepares a one-page note for a two-month pilot.
Demonstrate.stock_query: row of rental bicycles in european city

Demonstrate.voiceover: Her scope is bike availability, prices and opening hours. Everything else goes to a person. Her measures are the four you just saw, compared with the two months before launch. Her warning signs include chats that end after one message, repeat contacts within two days, and any complaint that the assistant was hard to leave.

slide.title: Sofie's launch note: part 1
slide.body: Scope: availability, prices, opening hours; everything else → a person. Measures: response time, resolution, hand-off rate, satisfaction vs the two months before. Warning signs: one-message chats · repeat contact within two days · 'hard to leave' complaints.

Demonstrate.voiceover: For quality, a team member reads twenty random conversations each week, in all three languages. The welcome message says it is an AI assistant, and the data protection officer approves what data is collected. She reviews quality weekly, the measures monthly, and after two months decides to continue, change or stop.

slide.title: Sofie's launch note: part 2
slide.body: Quality checks: 20 random conversations a week, all three languages, L11 checklist. Transparency and privacy: AI welcome message; data protection officer approves data. Review: weekly quality · monthly measures · decision after two months.

Demonstrate.voiceover: After the first month, containment is high, but satisfaction for French conversations is lower. Sofie reads those conversations and finds two French articles are missing. She adds them, and watches the next month's results.

slide.title: Reading the results
slide.body: Containment: high. Satisfaction: lower for French chats (highlighted). Cause found by reading conversations: two French articles missing → added.

Demonstrate.voiceover: A common mistake is to report only one number, the conversations the assistant handled. That rewards keeping customers away from people. Report containment with resolution and satisfaction, and treat a well-timed hand-off as good service.
Demonstrate.on_screen_text: A good hand-off is good service

Recap.voiceover: Let's recap. First, track response time, resolution, hand-off rate and satisfaction together, compared with your own results. Second, high containment is not always good, because customers who give up also count. Third, tell customers they are talking to AI, make a person easy to reach, and collect only the data you need.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. Four measures, read together, vs your own baseline. 2. High containment can hide customers who gave up. 3. Say it's AI · a person is easy to reach · only the data you need.

CTA.voiceover: Congratulations, you have finished the course! You designed a working assistant with a real hand-off to a human. For capstone step four, make your final fixes and write your one-page launch note. Then check the rubric checklist and submit your capstone: your assistant, your hand-off flow, your test sheet and your launch note. Well done, and keep the human touch.
